canonicalObjective: Establish and validate a deterministic, fail-closed anti-invention layer that prevents governed outputs, evidence, probabilities, statuses, claims, artifacts and conclusions from being accepted when they are fabricated, unsupported, non-reproducible, circular, hardcoded, stale, contradictory or not traceable to authoritative inputs.
objective: Establish and validate a deterministic, fail-closed anti-invention layer that prevents governed outputs, evidence, probabilities, statuses, claims, artifacts and conclusions from being accepted when they are fabricated, unsupported, non-reproducible, circular, hardcoded, stale, contradictory or not traceable to authoritative inputs.
strategicPurpose: Protect every downstream governance decision from invented support. A governed claim may pass only when its required support is authoritative, reproducible, provenance-bound and valid for the applicable contract; absence, ambiguity or contradiction of required evidence must block the claim.

basis: The canonical registry declares GATE14.nextGate = GATE15.
The sealed GATE14 R0005 checkpoint identifies GATE15 readiness planning as the next exact action.
No additional predecessor or hidden prerequisite is introduced by this mandate.

entryConditions: GATE14 is COMPLETE_CONFIRMED under the canonical ledger and sealed state lineage.
GATE15 is NOT_STARTED before the separate authorization and START mission.
R8 and all later GEE revisions are absent and unauthorized.
The canonical active-gate semantics remain unchanged; this mandate does not switch ACTIVE_GATE.
The implementation mission receives a separate exact contract, authority and path manifest.

definitions.governedClaim: A status, verdict, probability, confidence, evidence statement, artifact identity or derived conclusion that can influence a governed decision.
definitions.authoritativeEvidence: Evidence whose source identity, bytes, hash, revision, provenance and applicable contract are independently resolvable.
definitions.observedEvidence: Evidence actually obtained from an authoritative source and never synthesized from a summary or expectation.
definitions.derivedOutput: An output computed from declared authoritative inputs by a deterministic validator with traceable dependencies.
definitions.invention: Any unsupported, fabricated, synthetic, circular, stale, contradictory, hardcoded or untraceable value presented as a governed fact or verdict.

functionalRequirements.requirement: Detect and reject unsupported PASS or status claims.
Detect and reject hardcoded validation success that is not derived from the governed inputs.
Detect and reject missing authoritative sources.
Detect and reject source and evidence hash mismatches.
Detect and reject circular validation and self-attestation.
Detect and reject synthetic evidence presented as observed evidence.
Detect and reject invented probabilities or confidence values.
Detect and reject invented timestamps, revisions or identities.
Detect and reject derived outputs that cannot be traced to authoritative inputs.
Detect and reject contradictory evidence without silently choosing one authority.
Detect and reject stale evidence represented as current evidence.
Detect and reject missing required evidence.
Detect and reject evidence mutated after validation or after the evidence identity was bound.

requiredArtifacts.role: Validator identity, input, output and provenance registry
Positive, negative, counter and hostile tests
Machine-derived provenance, replay and closure evidence

validators.name: authoritative-source-binding-validator
validators.purpose: Resolve the declared authoritative source and bind its exact bytes, hash, revision and identity.
validators.requiredVerdict: PASS only when every required source binding is proven; otherwise BLOCKED.

validators.name: claim-provenance-validator
validators.purpose: Trace each governed claim and derived output to authoritative inputs and declared transformations.
validators.requiredVerdict: PASS only when the complete provenance chain is present and reproducible.

validators.name: evidence-freshness-and-identity-validator
validators.purpose: Reject stale, contradictory, mutated or identity-mismatched evidence.
validators.requiredVerdict: BLOCKED for any unresolved freshness, identity, hash or contradiction defect.

validators.name: deterministic-verdict-validator
validators.purpose: Ensure the verdict and rejection reason code are derived from the same bytes on replay and in a fresh process.
validators.requiredVerdict: PASS only when replay bytes, verdict and reason codes are identical.

validators.name: anti-circularity-validator
validators.purpose: Reject producer self-attestation, circular evidence and validator output reused as its own authority.
validators.requiredVerdict: BLOCKED when the authority chain is circular or self-generated.

validators.name: anti-invention-coverage-validator
validators.purpose: Recompute coverage of every mandatory anti-invention class and closure condition.
validators.requiredVerdict: PASS only when all mandatory classes are covered by real validator executions and evidence.

positiveTests.case: authoritative evidence with matching bytes, hash, identity, revision and provenance
complete derived claim whose inputs and transformations are fully traceable
identical replay in a fresh process with identical canonical bytes
positiveTests.expected: PASS with identical verdict and evidence digest

positiveTests.case: independent validator invocation over an unchanged evidence package

negativeTests.mutation: replace observed evidence with fabricated bytes
claim PASS without the required validation result
hardcode a successful verdict while changing the required input
change evidence bytes without changing the bound hash
make the validator output its own authority input
label a synthetic fixture as observed evidence
insert a probability or confidence value without authoritative support
invent a timestamp, revision or identity not present in authoritative evidence
remove one input edge from a derived output provenance chain
supply contradictory authoritative evidence without a canonical resolution
present evidence older than the applicable as-of boundary as current
modify evidence after its validation identity was bound

countertests.mutation: replace a real computed result with a literal PASS
countertests.expected: the countertest detects the hardcoded success

countertests.mutation: change one authoritative input byte and replay
countertests.expected: the affected claim blocks with a deterministic reason code

countertests.mutation: remove, duplicate or redirect one source edge
countertests.expected: the graph validator blocks and reports the exact defect

countertests.mutation: replace an observed source with a same-shape synthetic fixture
countertests.expected: synthetic evidence is rejected as observed evidence

countertests.mutation: replay the same package in a separate process and working directory
countertests.expected: the result is byte-identical and no ambient state changes the verdict

hostileTests.attack: tamper with a sealed evidence member after validation
tamper with a source hash while preserving a PASS field
use a producer-generated summary as the only authority
inject an unknown property or unsupported verdict into the evidence package
reorder, duplicate or remove mandatory requirement identities
hostileTests.expected: BLOCKED by coverage and identity validation

hostileTests.attack: use future-dated evidence for an earlier as-of claim

evidenceRequirements.requirement: Every authoritative input is identified by exact repository or declared external identity, SHA-256 and byte length.
Every governed claim has a complete source-to-output provenance chain and declared transformation.
Every freshness-sensitive item has an explicit as-of boundary and ordered timestamp or revision evidence.
Positive, negative, counter and hostile executions record raw inputs, raw outputs, verdict, reason code, process identity and exact artifact hashes.
Closure evidence is machine-derived from real validator executions and cannot be supplied by a producer summary alone.

closureConditions.condition: All mandatory anti-invention classes are covered exactly once or with an explicit non-duplicate mapping.
Real production validators exist and every declared validator is exercised.
Valid authoritative cases are accepted with complete provenance.
Negative and hostile invention cases are rejected fail-closed.
closureConditions.expectedResult: all mandatory negative and hostile tests BLOCK with the declared reason code

closureConditions.condition: Countertests prove the validators are not hardcoded, circular or summary-only.
closureConditions.expectedResult: all countertests PASS and no hardcoded or circular verdict survives

closureConditions.condition: Deterministic replay produces identical verdicts, reason codes and evidence digests.
Evidence provenance and exact source identity validate independently.
No unexpected repository or governance writes occur during validation.
closureConditions.expectedResult: unexpectedWriteCount = 0 and changedPaths are within the separately authorized implementation manifest

closureConditions.condition: No new unrelated regression identity is introduced.
GATE14 remains COMPLETE_CONFIRMED and immutable, no later gate is authorized, and R8 remains absent.
closureConditions.expectedResult: predecessorStateUnchanged = true, laterGateAuthorizationCount = 0 and R8 = ABSENT

forbiddenScope: real orders, broker writes, network calls, Git push and history rewrite
determinismRequirements: Run offline and locally from any working directory with no network dependency.
Use canonical JSON and exact byte hashing for all persisted identity claims.
Use stable, enumerated rejection reason codes; never derive a verdict from message wording or object order.
The same input bytes, contract and evidence identity produce the same verdict, reason code and evidence digest.
Recompute in a fresh process and preserve explicit as-of ordering; never infer currentness from wall-clock time alone.
Generated projections and producer summaries are never treated as independent authority.
failClosedRequirements: Missing, unknown, ambiguous or contradictory mandatory evidence is BLOCKED and never PASS.
A missing source, hash, revision, identity, provenance edge or required artifact is BLOCKED.
A producer cannot validate its own output or promote a summary into canonical authority.
Synthetic fixtures are clearly classified and cannot be represented as observed evidence.
A stale or future-incompatible item cannot be represented as current.
No placeholder, hardcoded PASS or fabricated counter is admissible.
downstreamGuarantees: A downstream gate may consume a GATE15 PASS only when each required claim is traceable to authoritative reproducible evidence.
A GATE15 PASS does not authorize START, execution, closure, external confirmation, ACTIVE_GATE switching or any later gate.
Gate16 can independently recompute the validator, provenance, mutation and replay evidence without trusting the producer summary.
No trading probability, market decision, broker action or dashboard behavior is produced by GATE15.

sourceReferences.evidence: The canonical registry names GATE15 Anti-invention validators and places it immediately after GATE14.
The sealed GATE14 checkpoint identifies GATE15 readiness planning as the next exact action after COMPLETE_CONFIRMED.
The constitutional rules require authoritative paths, no hardcoded PASS, no circular validation, no future leakage and no mandate redefinition.
Existing GEE primitives require canonical resolver use, deterministic local operations, hostile validation and evidence-bound readiness.

fieldBindings.rule: The two fields are byte-identical; canonicalObjective is the registry binding and objective is the explicit mandate field.
